Time immemorial, and still are, a Corporation; and, in Right thereof, they are seised in Fee of Lands, and have Time immemorially received the Rents, Issues, and Profits thereof, as also of an Estate called Town Farms, distinguished by the Titles of Great Farms, Penny Halfpenny, Sheep Market, Tolfery, and -con-

siding of ftnall Customary Dues or Payments , and also of ftnall Fines, which said Dues and Fines are paid by -Persons not being Free Burgeflees, or otherwise customarily exempted; and that the Petitioners and their Predecessors have repaired, sustained, and maintained, many Edifices and Buildings, within the said Borough and Parish, made Use of by Persons trading to or from the said Port, or frequenting the Markets and Fairs within the said Borough and Parish; and that the Yearly Revenues of the said Corporation, exclusive of the said Town Farms, are very inconsiderable, confiding mostly of small high Rents for Houses, held of them by Lease for long Terms of Years, and the accidental Fines arising from such Leases, which are by no Means sufficient for the Purposes intended; and that, in some Years, the Damages done to the Quays and public Buildings have been so sudden and great, by the Tide and high Winds, that Monies have been borrowed, from Time to Time, for the Support and Maintenance thereof, and of the other Buildings; and that the Quays alone cod them lad Year much more than all the certain Annual Income of their Revenue, and in all Probability will be attended with further considerable Expences, it being at this Time necessary to enlarge some of the Quays, and to build a Wall, or make other Conveniences, for keeping out the Tide; and that at present the Weekly Markets are all held in the High Street, under large Penthouses, or Sheds fixed to the Houses, which extend so far over the said Street, as to become a great Nuisance, and very inconvenient to Passengers, and which ought to be entirely taken away, or reduced considerably; to remedy which, the Petitioners are desirous, if their Estates and Dues shall be sufficient, and are confirmed to them, to build a Market Place, for the Sale of Butchers Meat, near the High Street, for the Convenience of the Town and Country; and that a considerable Sum of Money mud now be laid out on the several Works and Buildings aforesaid, besides the Money already expended thereon; and that it will be necessary for the Petitioners to borrow and take up a Sum of Money, on the Credit of their said- Estates,

Farms, Tolls, and Dues, for the Purposes aforesaid:

And therefore praying. That, for making the said Tolls and Dues an unquestionable Security to the Lenders, they may be at Liberty to bring in a Bill for confirming to them and their Success'ors the said Farms,

Estate, ancient Tolls, and Dues, so immemorially received by the Petitioners; and for building a Market Place in the said Town, and enlarging the said Quays, and other the Purposes aforesaid; and that they may be at Liberty to borrow and take up at Interest a Sum of Money, on the Credit of the said Farms, Estates, Tolls, and Dues, in Manner before set forth, for the public Uses and Purposes aforesaid.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

A Petition of the Merchants and Manufacturers of Ditar. the Towns of Manchester and Warrington, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That many-valuable and important Articles of Commerce are, and have been from Time immemorial, manufactured in those Towns and the Countries adjacent, to the great Emolument of this Kingdom in general, and entire Support of some Hundred Thousands of His Majesty’s Subjects, who are wholly dependant thereon; and that the flourishing State of the neighbouring Port of Liverpool is of the utmost Consequence to the Petitioners, as a principal Channel through which these Manufactures are conveyed to Foreign Markets; and that the Petitioners are informed, that the Merchants of Liverpool have applied for a Bill, to enable them to raise a Fund, to be applied to the Support and Encouragement of Commerce, by levying a small Tax upon Goods and Merchandize landed within the said Port; and the Petitioners are persuaded, and believe, that the Establishment of such a Fund will be of real and important Utility: And therefore praying, That the said Bill may pass into a Law.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Liverpool Petition of the Merchants of the Port of Liverpool, Port whose Names are subscribed, was presented to the House, Dues. and read; Setting forth. That the very great Attention shewn by the House to the Commercial Interests of this Kingdom, renders it frequently necessary to fend up some of their own Body from that Town to attend, during the Sitting of Parliament, on Matters of Trade, where the Interest of the Nation in general, and of this Port in particular, are immediately concerned; and that, by the great Distance of that Place from the Metropolis, the Joumies and Attendance of such Deputations occasion an unavoidable and heavy Expence; and that, above 40 Years ago, an Agreement was voluntarily entered into, by the Merchants of that Place, to admit a small Duty to be levied upon all Goods from America, for the Purpose of railing a Fund, to defray the Charge of Attendances on Parliament, and any other public Expences tending to promote and secure thd Trade of Liverpool-,which Duty was accord-

ingly collected for about 30. Years, during which Time many important Advantages accrued to the Public from the Application of such Fund to the Interest and Purposes for which it was raised; and that, within a few Years part, several Persons haverefufed the Payment of this Contribution, as partially levied upon the African and American Traders only, though all the Merchants of the Port and their European Correspondents were equally benefited; and that the Petitioners apprehend, many unavoidable Disadvantages will certainly arise, from the want of a Fund to defray the Expences aforesaid: And therefore praying. That a Bill may be brought in, to levy a small Duty upon all Goods and Merchandizes imported or brought Coastways into Liverpool, for the general Service of the said Port, under such Regulations and Restrictions as to the House shall seem meet.

A Motion was made, and the Question being put. That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House;

The House divided.

Linen Trade. A Petition of the Printers of Linens, Cottons, and (Caiiko printer, Callicoes, residing near London, whole Names are there-Undoo.) unto subscribed, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners perceive, by the Votes, that the State of the Linen Trade of Great Britain and Ireland is ordered to be taken into Consideration; and are informed, that an Application for additional Duties upon the Importation of Foreign Linens, and a further Retention of Duties upon Exportation of those Linens when printed, is intended; and that the Printing Trade is a very valuable Manufactory to this Kingdom, and pays a considerable Revenue in Excise, and has been greatly extended by the Printing of Foreign Linens for Exportation; and that, in case any additional Duties should be laid, or further Drawbacks retained on Exportation, the Petitioners would be deprived of a very considerable Part of their Trade, which has been upon the Decline for several Years: And therefore praying the House to take the Premises into Consideration, and that they may be heard, by themselves or Counsel, against any Regulations that may be offered to be made, in the Linen Trade, that may affect them. A Petition of Major General Simon Frafer, being offered to be presented to the House;

The Lord North, by His Majesty’s Command, acquainted the House, that His Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, gives His Consent, as far as His Majesty’s Interest is concerned; and recommends the same to the Consideration of the House:

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; Setting forth. That, by an Act, passed in the Twenty-fifth Year of his late Majesty’s Reign, for annexing certain forfeited Estates to the Crown, all and every the Estates whatsoever which became forfeited to his said late Majesty, by the Attainder of Simon late Lord were

unalienably annexed to the Crown of these Realms; and that, sensible as the Petitioner is of the Propriety of the said Act, he hopes his particular same will appear to the House so distinguished from others, as that it may be made an Exception; and that, in the Year 1747, Proof was brought before Parliament of the Means used to involve the Petitioner in the late unnatural Rebellion, at an Age which made it impossible for him to refill such Means; and that, for some Time before the Attainder of the said Simon late Lord Lovat, his Estates were settled by a Deed of Entail, which came to Trial before the Court of Session in Scotland, and upon which the Judges were so divided in Opinion, that the Estate was determined to be forfeited by a Majority of One Voice only; and though some of the ablest Counsel in England advised an Appeal from that Judgment, yet no Appeal was brought, in Deference to the Views which Government then entertained with respect to such Estates, and in Hopes that Time would afford an Opportunity to the Petitioner of recommending his Cale to the public Favour; and that the Petitioner having been lent to GlaJ'gow at Ten Years of Age, was from that Time always educated under Mailers the moll distinguished for Zeal and Attachment to the Constitution and Government of this Country; and he proved his Adherence to the Principles of that Education, by rejecting the Offer of a Regiment in the French Service immediately after the Rebellion, when he had nothing to rely on but the Hope he entertained of becoming a useful Subject of this Country, by dedicating his Life to its Service; and that he took the earliest Opportunity of soliciting to be employed at the Beginning of the last War, and was soon after called upon to quit a Profession which he had embraced as the moll independent Situation in Time of profound Peace, he raised in a few Weeks 1,800 Men, and had the Honour to-command a Regiment composed of them, with which he served during the Courl'e of the War in America; and it was his good Fortune to be the first who offered to set that Example, which, in its Consequences, proved advantageous to the State, by calling forth from a Corner of the Kingdom, many Thousand Soldiers, who, in every Quarter of the Globe, contributed to the Glory and Success of that War; and that the Petitioner has arrived at the Rank of Major General in His

A. 1774.

Majesty’s Service, and, since the Peace, has been-employed, by His Majesty’s Commands, in the Service of a Power whose Alliance this Country has always deemed important: And therefore praying, for Leave to bring in a Bill, to enable His Majesty to grant to the Petitioner the Estate which belonged to the said late

Lord Lovat, and which was annexed to the Crown by the said Act of the Twenty-fifth Year of his late Majesty’s Reign, subject to such A nnual Quit Rent as to the House shall appear just and reasonable.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee of the whole House.

Resolved, That this House will, upon Friday Morning next, resolve itself into a Committee of the whole House, to consider of the said Petition.

A Petition of the High Sheriff, Grand Jury, and Gentlemen, of the County Palatine of Durham, at the Affixes holden at the City of Durham, on the Third Day of August 1773, was presented to the House, and read; Reciting several Provisions in the Acts made for apprehending Highwaymen, Burglars, and Persons guilty of Offences within the Act commonly called " The Black " Act;" and Setting forth. That, by an Act, made in the Third Year of the Reign of his late Majesty King George the First, for the better regulating the Office of Sheriffs, and for ascertaining their Fees, and the Fees for filing out their Patents and passing their Accounts, Provision is made for re-paying the Sheriffs the Money they shall disburse in Payment of such Rewards, immediately upon the same being so disbursed; and that the Petitioners apprehend, that, on the making of the said several Acts of Parliament, the Legislature intended that the same should be general* and extend to all the Counties ard Cities of this Kingdom; but the Judges who have come the Northern Circuit, upon being applied to for Certificates of the Conviction of such Offenders in the said County, in order to entitle the Appre-henders, and Convidlors of them to such Rewards, have always refused to give such Certificates, thinking that the said several Acts do not extend to the said County, as the Sheriff of the said County is not the Sheriff of, or appointed by, the Grown, but has been immemorially appointed, by Patent, by the Bishop of and has

no Accounts to pass or keep with His Majesty; and which Idea having become too univerlally known, the said County has in several Instances, and may in many others, become a Place of Refuge for the most desperate and determined Villains; and that the Petitioners and all the other Inhabitants of the said County contribute equally with others to the Support of Government, by the Payment of all public Taxes and Levies, and other Duties, and therefore conceive they are equally entitled to the Protection thereof in their Persons and Properties: And therefore praying the House to take the Matter into Consideration, and to give Leave for bringing in a Bill, to make the said several Acts of Parliament, with respect to the Rewards to be given for apprehending Highwaymen and other Offenders therein-mentioned, extend to the said County Palatine, and so that the Judge, before whom any such Offender shall be convicted, may have a Power, by his Certificate, to ascertain and fix the Money to be paid as a Reward, at any Sum not exceeding Forty Pounds, nor less than Ten Pounds, as in his Discretion he shall think fit; and that the Petitioners may be thereby relieved, in the Matters aforesaid, in such Manner as the House shall think fit.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine, and Hate to the House, the Matter of FaCl contained in the said Petition:

And it is referred to Sir Thothas Clavering, Sir White Ridley, &c.: And they are to meet Tomorrow Morning, at Nine of the Clock, in the Speaker’s Chamber ;. and have Power to lend for Persons, Papers, and Records.

The Lord Advocate of Scotland reported from the Ayr Committee, to whom the Petition of the rrioft noble Bank. Henry Duke of Buc'cleugh, and the most noble Charles Duke of Queensbury and Dover, in Behalf of themselves and the other Copartners of the Bariking Company, iri that Part of Great Britain called Scotland; known under the Firm of Douglas, Heron, and Company, was referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of Fact contained in the said Petition; and had directed him to report a State thereof to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it jp at the Clerk’s Table: Where th& same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

A State of the Matter of Fact contained in the said Petition, is as follows:

It apj>eared by the Evidence of Robert Mayne, Esquire Banker in London, That the Petitioners and others dict in the Year 1769, enter into Partnership, for carrying on the Banking Business in Scotland, and subscribed a Capital of 160,000 for that Purpose; and that he has been their principal Correspondent in London, ever since they commenced Business, in November 1769.

That in June 1772, the Partnership were reduced tb the utmost Distress, for want of Money to pay their Bills then becoming due from Day to Day, owing to the great Quantity of Bills they had then running on them, and to the Failure of many Houses here, and in Scotland, at that Time.

That such of the Managers of the said Company,' ak were then in London, finding it impossible for them tp pay their Bills, without railing Money for that Purpose by Sale of Annuities, were for some Time extremely doubtful, Whether they should submit to this unprofitable Method' of saving themselves, or flop Payment, which at that critical Time, when Public Credit had ipet With so severe a Check, would have occasioned the Failure of many Companies both in Scotland and England, with1 Whom they werC connected; but that after much Chn-fiderdtion, they thought it would be more for the Interest of Public Credit, to raise Money by Sale of Annuities, upon the very disadvantageous Terms mentioned in the Proposals set forth in the Petition, rather than fuffcr fa many People to be distressed on their account; and that: accordingly, in June 1772, and the.Two following Months, they raised ^.450,000 and upwatds, by Sale of Annuities; and a great Part of the Money raised by such Sale, wal applied to the Payment of such of their Bills as were' payable at his House; and that the Transe action respecting the raising of Moneyby Sale of Annuities, was approved of by the Company, at their next General Meeting, in November 1772.

That the Witness has paid the Annuitants their Aiv nuities, as they became due, ever since; and knows the Amount of the Sum raised was £.450,000 and upwards, for which they pay near 60,000 a Year: That he was present at a General Meeting of the Proprietors, held at Edinburgh, in Augtift last, when they came to a unanimous ltesolution of giving up the Business of Banking; and the Persons mentioned in the Petition, or any Three of* them, were then appointed a Committee, for managing and winding up their Affairs; and thal at another'

General Meeting, held in December last. Sir Adolphus Oughton, and Messieurs Lockhart and Syme, were added to the said Committee.

That the Witness has in his Possession, the original Proposals made to the Annuitants, which are exactly the same as stated in the Petition, and are'signed and accepted by a considerable Number of the Annuitants; and another Copy of the said Proposals is lodged in the Hands of Richard Glover, Esquire, which is likewise signed by^a considerable Number of the Annuitants;

It appeared to your Committee by an Act, made in the Parliament of Scotland, in the Year 1695, intituled,

" An Act for erecting a Bank in Scotland," That a Joint Stock amounting to £.1,200,000 Scots, or £.100,000 Sterling, was allowed to be raised and paid in Manner therein directed; and that £.1000 Scots should be the lowest, and £.20,000 Scots the highest.

Sum which any One Person should be allowed to subscribe. — And by the said Act it was declared, That the Persons subscribing to the said Stock should be a Body Corporate and Politic, by the Name of The Governor and Company of the Bank of Scotland-, under which Name they were to have perpetual Succession, and a Common ,-

Seal; and certain Rules were prescribed for the better ordering and Management of their Affairs.

A Petition of the Merchants of the City of Bristol trading to Germany and Holland, and dealing in Linens imported from those Countries, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Petitioners are informed, Application has been made, to lay an additional Duty upon all Linens imported into- this Kingdom from Germany or Holland, without allowing any Drawbacks on Exportation; which* if allowed, the Petitioners apprehend, Mealiujes may be taken Abroad, to lay Imposts- upon the Manufactures of this Kingdom, which may not only deprive great Numbers of the Poor Manufacturers of the Means of providing for themselves and Families, but alia leften the Demand for the Goods and Produce of Inch Manufactures; and that the Exportation of such Foreign Linen- may be abridged, and that Branch of Business be inevitably thrown into the Hand's of Foreign Powers, Rivals in the Trade of this Kingdom: And therefore praying the House, to take the Pre-, mises into Consideration, and prevent the Evils so justly apprehended.

Carnarvon Mr. Williams reported from the Committee, to whom Sea Shore the Petition of the Gentlemen, Clergy, Land Owners, OrnwHead anC^ Occupiers the several Messuages, Tenements, r’d e Lands, and Premises, near and adjoining to the Sea Voryd River. Shore between the Orms Head, in the County of Carnarvon, and the River at Voryd, which bounds the several Counties of Flint and Denbigh, was referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition; and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and lie read the Report in his Place, and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk’s Table: Where the same was read) and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, your Committee called Mr. William Lloyd j who, being Vol. 34.

examined, said, That from Orms Head to Poryd is about Twelve measured Miles along the Sea Coast, where the Tide flows very rapidly; that, for upwards of Three Miles, the Banks are, from 14 to 20 Yards perpendicular, above High Water Mark, of a Clay or Marly Nature, or soft Loam, mixed with Stones; that at the Foot of those Banks there Were, some Years ago, avail Quantity of Stones, which prevented the Tide from wash ing the Banks away; but of late Years the common People have broke the large Stones, and, together with the lmaller ones, laid them on Heaps, and fold them to the Masters of Vessels for Ballast; by which Means the Tide flows higher, and many Acres of valuable Land, and Part of the Road from Chester to Holyhead, have been washed away.

And he produced to your Committee a Plan, shewing how much Land had been loft by the aforesaid Means. And,

A Member present confirmed that Part of his Evidence. And,

Mr. Lloyd, being further examined, said. That he brought Actions, as an Attorney, for the Landholders, against the Persons who pick Stones on the Coast; and that, although the Proof of the Damage done to the Lands was clear, the Judges and Counsel were in Doubt as to the Legality of the Actions, and recommended it to the Plaintiffs to wave the Cpfts, and accept of a Ver-di£l, which they agreed to do, as the Defendants were, very poor; that some of the Defendants not appearing to the Action, Attachments were sued out, and they were arrested and imprisoned for want of entering an Appearance, by which their Families became a Burthen to the Parishes; notwithstanding which, the common People still continue doing the fame, to the great Detriment of the Landowners, and-Inhabitants; and, unless some Method be taken to prevent them, many Hundred Acres of the bell Corn Land in North Wales, and great Part of the Road from Holyhead to Saint Asaph, will be carried away by the Sea. Then,

Mr. Grearfon, the proper Officer, produced

to your Committee Two Records of Verdicts given as aforesaid in the Court of Exchequer. And,

Mr. Lloyd added further, That by prosecuting Actions at Law, the lower Class of People wili be undoubtedly ruined, and large Sums expended, without any Remedy for the Evils complained of.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill to prevent the taking and carrying away of Stones from the Sea Shore, below High Water Mark, between Orms Head, in the County of Carnarvon, and the River at Voryd: And that Mr. Williams, Sir Roger Moflyn, and Mr; Hill, do prepare, and bring in, the lame.

A Petition of the Merchants of London, trading to the linen Trade. British Sugar Colonies, was presented to the House, and (Sugar Colo-read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners are Exporters of Goods to the Sugar Colonies in most Branches of the British Manufactures, and of British and Foreign Linens to a considerable Amount, necessary for the Use and Trade of the Inhabitants of those Colonies; and that the Petitioners have been informed of an intended Application, for Leave to bring in a Bill to alter the present Duties and Drawbacks on Foreign Linens; and the Petitioners are of Opinion, that, in case an Act should pass to increase the Duties on Foreign Linens, without allowing the Drawback of such Duties, it will greatly encourage the clandestine Importation of Foreign Linens into His Majesty’s Sugar Colonies, and with them many other Foreign Manufactures: And therefore praying, That the above Measure may not be adopted by the House.

A Petition of the Gentlemen, Merchants, Manufacturers, and Traders, of the Town and Neighbourhood of Rochdale, was also presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners are informed, that it is intended to lay an additional Duty upon Foreign Linens imported^ and that the Petitioners apprehend, that the laying an additional Impoftupon Foreign Linens imported, would.oocasion the imposing of such Duties upon Engl/fhWoollens, and also upon Foreign Raw

Hemp and Flax, as would be very injurious and detrimental to the Trade and Manufactures of the Kingdom in general, and of the Petitioners in particular: And therefore praying. That a Bill for the Purpose of laying an additional Duty upon Foreign Linens imported, may not pass into a Law.

A Petition of the Merchants and Manufacturers of the Town and Neighbourhood of Manchester, in the County Palatine of Lancaster, was also presented to the

House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners are under the great eft Apprehensions, that an additional Duty will be propefed on Foreign Linens, with a Retention of the said Duty on their Exportation to our Colonies i and that the Manufacture of Cotton Goods has greatly increasedduriqg the last Seven Years, principally . owing to the many Improvements which have been made therein, without the Aid of any Bounty; and that, in consequence of such Improvements, very large Quantities of the said Manufactures have been exported to those - Foreign Countries from whence Linens are imported, by which Means tire Consequences apprehended from the late Spanish Prohibition, have 'been in a great Measure

prevented; and that the Duties imposed on our Manufactures in the Countries from whence Linens are imported, are very moderate; and that the Petitioners have Realbn to believe, that the Value of British Commodities exported to those Countries far exceeds the Value of the Linens imported from thence; and consequently have. Cause to fear the Effects of a Foreign Retaliation, which may prove highly prejudicial to the Manufactures , of England in general, and to those of the Petitioners in particular: And therefore praying the House, to take the Premises into Consideration, and that the Petitioners may be heard, touching the lame.

And the said Petitions were severally ordered to be referred to the Consideration of the Committee of the whole House, to whom it is referred to enquire further into the present Stale of the Linen Trade in Great Britain and Ireland.

to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Petitioner, having justly incurred the Displeasure of the House, by printing a Letter, highly, falsely, and unjustly, reflecting on the Character of the Speaker of this/

House, was summoned to attend on Monday the 14th of February last; and that the Petitioner did readily obey that Summons, and did attend the House accordingly; and that the Petitioner h^s offended inadvertently* and through a very blameable Neglect of not carefully examining, as he ought to have done, the Contents of what he printed; which Kind of Neglect he will in future use his utmost Endeavours to avoid: And that the Petitioner has already incurred very heavy Expences, which, if long continued, must end in the Ruin of himself, and a numerous and innocent Family, who must be Sufferers together with him: And therefore praying.

rend Thomas Jennings, Clerk, the Sub-tutor or Ulher of the said School, was referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition; and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk’s Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr. John Stafford produced to your Committee, Letters Patent of King Edward the Sixth, bearing Date the 25th Day of April, in the Sixth Year of his Reign, for founding a Free Grammar School in Macclesfield, for the Iri-struction of Youth, under the Directions and Regulations therein expressed; by which Patent he also incorporated Fourteen Persons to be Governors of the Pof-sessions. Revenues, and Goods, of the said School; and also granted to them several Estates there, of the then yearly Value of £.21. $s. with Power to appoint k Mailer and Ulhers, as Vacancies might happen; and expressly ordaining. That the whole Revenues should be appropriated to the sustaining a Mailer and Ulher of the said School only.

And the Witness said. That the old School and School-house being in great Decay, and inconveniently situated, the Governors, in the Year 1750, fold the lame, with a Piece of Land adjoining. Part of the said Trull Estate, and with the Money arising therefrom purchased a Messuage and Buildings thereto belonging, in Macclesfield, more commodious for the Purpose, together with a Close, and other small Pieces of Land.

And the Witness produced to your Committee, a Survey and Valuation of the said School Estates > by which it appeared, that the present Rent amounts to £. 180. 8i. 8 d. and the Value in Reversion after the Expiration of certain Leases outstanding on old Lives, will amount to £. 636. 8 s.6 d.: And he said. That some Parts of the said Estates consist of Houses and Buildings, which are very old and in Decay, the rebuilding or repairing of which will be attended with a considerable Expence; and other Parts consist of Lands dispersed, and intermixed with Lands of other Persons, which is attended with Inconvenience; but if Power was given to make Exchanges of such Lands, and to fell such Hotifes and Buildings as Opportunities offer, and the same shall be found expedient, it would greatly contribute to the Benefit of the Foundation.

Two Members present. Governors of the said School, informed your Committee, That great Benefit would arise to the Youth educated at the said School, and the Foundation be greatly improved, if they and their Successorswere enabled, as the Revenues of the School shall encrease, to appoint additional Mailers arid Ulhers, with suitable Salaries; with Power to remove or displace them' upon any just and reasonable Caule.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for confirming certain Purchases made by the Governors of the Poflessions, Revenues, and Goods, of the Free Grammar School ot King Edward the Sixth, in Macclesfield, within the Parish of Preftbury, in the County of Chester; to enable the said Governors to sell or exchange some other Parts of their Estates, and to lay out the Money arising by such Sales, and the other Revenues belonging to the said School, for the Benefit thereof; and VOL.34.

Mr. Symons reported from the Committee, to whom Hereford the Petition of the Mayor, Aldermen, and Citizens, Poor Gentlemen, Clergy, and Inhabitants, of the City of He- Petition-reford, was referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition; and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk’s Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth: viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Mr.

Lacon Lambe, being examined, said, that the Poor of the said City and Suburbs are very numerous, and are maintained at a great Expence; and that the Pavements of the Streets and Lanes within the Limits aforesaid are in- a very ruinous State, and dangerous for Passengers.

That if some further Provision was made for maintaining and regulating the Poor within the said City and Suburbs, and for paving, lighting, and cleansing, the Streets, Lanes, ana other Places, and preventing all Annoyances therein, it would be of great Benefit and Convenience to the Inhabitants, and all Persons resorting to the said City.

That the usual Fund for repairing the Streets and High Causeways in the said City, ariles from the Profits of a Common, called New Widemarsh, which is enjoyed by the Corporation of the said City, from Candlemas Day to Lammas Day Yearly, and by the Proprietors of Lands and Tenements in the Parish of Holmer, in the County of Hereford, for Three Months after Lammas Day every Year.

That there are two other Parcels of Waste Ground lying within the Liberties of the said City, called Old Widemarsh and Monck Moor, which are at present of very little Value, but if the same were inclosed and improved, the Profits thereof would, with the Aid of Two Assessments Yearly, of Six Pence in the Pound, on the Occupiers of all Houses, Buildings, and Gardens* within the said City and Suburbs, create a Fund sufficient for paving, lighting, and cleansing, the several Streets,

Lanes, and other Places, within the Limits aforesaid.

The Witness then produced to your Committee, a.

Decree, made in the Court of Chancery, bearing Date the i;rth of February 1763, in a Cause wherein the Attorney General, at the Relation of Francis Campbell, was Informant, and the Right honourable and Right Reverend James Lord Bishop of Hereford, and others, Defendants; whereby it appeared, that an Account was dire (fled to be taken of the Sum of £. 400, given by a Codicil to the Will of the late Lord Scudamore, as a perpetual Stock, to set to work the poor People of the City of Hereford; and the Charity was established; and it was referred to a Mailer in Chancery to approve a Scheme for Application of the Money; who made-his Report, dated 26 October 1764 (also produced to your Committee) and certified, that a Scheme had been laid before him, whereby it was proposed, that the Sum of "

A Petition of Henry Raines, James Smyth, Thomas Aire Mill* Feme, and Joseph Armitage, was presented to the House, Proprietor* and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners are Own- P«it»c. ers and Proprietors of several ancient Fulling, Rasping,

Grinding, and other Mills, employed in the Cloth Trade, and of Corn Mills, which have been erected Time immemorial, upon the River Air, in the West Riding of the County of York; and that the Petitioners observe, by the Votes, that a Petition hath been presented, by the Undertakers of the Navigation of the Rivers Air and Colder, for Leave to bring in a» Bill to enable them as well to extend and make all necessary Improvements in the Navigation of the said Rivers, as also to complete and support a Cut from the River Air, in or near the Township of Haddlefey, to the River Ouze, in or near the Township of Selby, in the said County; and that the Petitioners are informed, that, by the Evidence given before the Committee to whom the said Petition was referred, it appears, that various collateral new Navigable Cuts, of considerable Extent, are proposed to be made through the Lands adjoining to the said River Air, although, by an Advertisement published on the Behalf of the said Undertakers, uporr the 28th Day of December last, the said Undertakers thereby informed the Public, that they had consulted! able Engineers, who had given them the strongest Rea-fons to believe the Capability of rendering the Navigation of the said Rivers in the present Channel effectual and satisfactory, from whence the Petitioners were induced to believe they meant to improve the natural Channel or Bed of the Rivers, and did not intend to apply to Parliament for Powers to make any collateral Cuts; and the Petitioners were the more satisfied in their Apprehensions, upon reading the Undertakers Petition in the Votes, as there is not the least Mention of a Necessity of any collateral Cuts., nor any Prayer for Powers to make the same; and therefore the Petitioners submit, whether the Petition is not insufficient to support the Powers now desired, of making such collateral Cuts; and representing to the House, that the making such Cuts, and the several other Works mentioned in a Re^-port of Mr. Smeatons, as necessary to be done, for the Improvement of the said Navigation, will not only divert from, the Petitioners said Mills a very considerable;

Quantity of the Water which now flows down the River Air, but will, in many other Respects, be very prejudicial to the Properties of the Petitioners and other Milli Owners upon the said River Air:And therefore praying the House to take the Premises into Consideration, and that they may be heard, by themselves or Counsel, against the said Bill, in Support of the Allegations of their Petition, so that the whole Matter may be enquired into; and that nothing may be done to prejudice the ‘ said Mills, which are essentially necessary to the Continuance of the Woollen Manufactory within the said West Riding of York.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the-liable, until the Bill to amend an Act, passed in the

That the Petitioners are informed that a Bill is intended to be brought in, to lay an additional Duty on all Foreign Linens imported into this Kingdom; and that the Petitioners are apprehensive that such an additional Duty will greatly affect and injure the Woollen Trade of this Kingdom in general, and distress the Inhabitants of the said City in particular: And therefore praying the House to take the same into their Consideration.

Mr. Speaker left the Chair.

Sir Thomas Clavering took the Chair of the Committee.

Mr. Speaker resumed the Chair.

Sir Thomas Clavering reported from the Committee,

That they had examined several Witnesses; and had gone through the Bill; and made several Amendments thereunto; which they had directed him to report, when the House will please to receive the same.

Ordered, That the Report be received upon Monday Morning next.

Sir Thomas Clavering also reported from the said Mr. Howard, Committee, That he was directed by the Committee to move the House, That John Howard, Esquire, be called in to the Bar; and that Mr. Speaker do acquaint him, that this House are very sensible of the Humanity and Zeal which have led him to visit the several Gaols of this Kingdom, and to communicate to the House the interesting Observations he has made on that Subject.

And Sir Thomas Clavering moved the House accordingly.

Resolved, Nemint Contradicente, That John Howard,

Esquire, be called in to the Bar; and that Mr. Speaker do acquaint him, that this House are very sensible of the Humanity and Zeal which have led him to visit the several Gaols of this Kingdom, and to communicate to the House the interesting Observations he has made on that Subject.

John Howard, Esquire, was accordingly called in to the Bar; and Mr. Speaker acquainted him with the said Resolution.

And then he was directed to withdraw.

Linen A Petition of the Merchants, Exporters, and Manu-Trade fu&urers of Cloth and other Woollen Goods, in the (Wakefield).. Parish of Wakefield, in the West Riding of the County of York, whose Names are thereto subscribed, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners are fearful that an additional Duty on Foreign Linens, with a Retention of the Duty on their Exportation to our Colonies, will be proposed this Session; and that the Petitioners believe, that the Value ,ol British Woollen Goods exported to Foreign Parts

much exceeds the Value of Linens imported from thence; and, the Duties on our Manufactures in those Parts being moderate, the Petitioners have Reason to apprehend the Effects of a Foreign Retaliation would be highly 4

detrimental to the Petitioners, its well as to all other the Woollen Manufacturers in this Kingdom: And therefore praying the House will take the Premises into Consideration, and permit the Merchants, Exporters, and Manufacturers of Clodi and other Woollen Goods in this Kingdom, to be heard against any Innovations by additional Duty on Foreign Linens, or will grant them such other Relief as to the House may seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the Committee of the whole House, to whom it is referred to enquire further into the present State of the Linen Trade in Great Britain and Ireland.

GEORGE R.

His Majesty, upon Information of the unwarrantable Practices which have been lately concerted and carried on in North America, and particularly of the violent and outrageous Proceedings at the Town and Port of Bof- to the Earl of Dartmouth, dated Boston, die 4th of January ton, in the Province of Massachusets Bay, with a View 1774: Received the 13th of February: And also, to obstructing; he Commerce of this Kingdom, and upon ' N° 31. Extra A of a Letter from -Major General Grounds and Pretences immediately subversive of the to the Earl of Dartmouth, dated New Fork, the

Conuitution thereof, hath thought fit to lay the whole 3d of November 1773: Received the 10th of Matter before His Two Houses of Parliament, fully confiding as well in their Zeal for the Maintenance of His Majesty’s Authority, as in their Attachment to common interest and Welfare of all His Dominions, that they will not only enable His Majesty effectually to take such Measures as may be most likely to put an immediate Stop to the present Disorders, but will also take into their most serious Consideration, what further Regulations and permanent Provisions may be necessary to be established, for better securing the Execution of the Laws, and the just Dependence of the Colonies upon the Crown and Parliament of Great Britain. G. R.

THE Lord Advocate of Scotland presented to the House, according to Order, a Bill for carrying into Execution certain Proposals, made by the most Noble Henry Duke of Buccleugh, the most Noble Charles Duke of Queensberry and Dover, and others, for redeeming the Annuities granted by the Company of the Bank of Ayr, in that Part of Great Britain called Scotland, known under the Firm of " Douglas, Heron, and Compiny: " And the same was received; and read the First Time.

Resolved, That the Bill be read a Second Time.

Mr. Egerton reported from the Committee, to whom the Bill to enable Thomas Asheton, Esquire, and his Sons, and the Heirs Male of their Bodies, to take and use the Surname of Smith, pursuant to the Will of William Smith, Esquire, deceased, was committed; That the Committee had examined the Allegations of the Bill, and found the same to be true; and that the Committee had directed him to report the Bill to the House, without any Amendment: And he delivered the Bill in at the Clerk’s Table.

Ordered, That the Bill be ingrossed.

A Petition of the Mayor, Aldermen, and Citizens, of the City of Bath, in Council assembled, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Petitioners are informed, that Application is making for a Bill for making, amending, and repairing, a Road to be carried by a Bridge acr-ols the River Avon, from the present Road, near Bathford, and from thence to or neRr the Village of Hampton, and from thence to or near the Village of Bathwick, and from thence to the new Bridge lately built acrois the said River, near to the old Ferry; and representing to the House, that the Entrance of such intended Road into the City of Bath will be over a Bridge not wide enough to make it commodious; and that it will cross a Street of the most public Passage in the City, which, the Petitioners apprehend, will be at termed with great Inconvenience and Danger; and that tire making l'uch Road will be unnecessary, and greatly prejudicial to many Individuals, and to the said City in general: And therefore praying. That the Petitioners may be heard, by their Counsel, against the passing of any Bill for the Purposes aforesaid; and that the Petitioners may have such Relief in the Premises as to the House shall feetn meet.

A Petition of the Trustees appointed in and by an Act of Parliament, passed in the Eighth Year of the Reign of His present Majesty, intituled, "An Act for " continuing the Terms of several Acts, made in the " Thirteenth Year of King George the First, and in the " Seventeenth and Thirty-second Years of his late Majesty, for repairing several Roads leading from and " through Chippenham, and from Chippenham Bridge, in the County of Wilts, and for amending the said Acts, " and reducing them into One Act of Parliament," was also presented to the House, and read; likewise taking Notice of the said Application; and Setting forth, That

1774.

the Petitioners have borrowed 3,500l. upon the Credit of the said Act, which has been expended in repairing the said Roads; and that the said Roads comprehend Nine Miles of the direct Poll Road from London to Bath, and communicate with sundry other Turnpike Roads leading into different Parts of Wiltshire and; and

that the Petitioners apprehend, if the said Bill should pass into a Law, the new Road to be made thereby would occasion a considerable Diversion of the Roads now in Use, without any equivalent Advantage to the Public, Whereby, the Petitioners apprehend, their Tolls would so much diminish, that they should not be able to keep the said Roads in Repair, and pay the Interest of the Money borrowed: And therefore praying, That they may be heard, by their Counsel, against the said Bill; and that they may have such Relief in the Premises as to the House shall seem meet.

ing in Repair, the Road from The Croft Keys, otherwise Brickers Barn, in the Parish of Corsham, fa the " County of Wilts, to Bath Bridge, in the County of Somerset," was also presented to the House, and read; likewise taking Notice of the said Application; and Setting forth, That the Petitioners have borrowed £.5,000 upon the Credit of the said Act, which has been expended in repairing the said Roads; and that the said Roads comprehend Five Miles of the direct Post Road from London to Bath, and communicate with lundry other Turnpike Roads leading into different Parts of Wiltshire and Somersetshire; and that the Petitioners apprehend, if the said Bill should pass into a Law, the new Road to be made thereby would occasion a considerable Diversion of the Roads now in Use, without an equivalent Advantage to the Public, whereby, the Petitioners apprehend, their Tolls would lo much diminish, that they should not be able to keep the said Roads in Repair, and pay the Interest of the Money borrowed: And therefore praying, That they may be heard, by their Counsel, against the said Bill; and that they may have such Relief in the Premises as to the House shall seem meet.

And the said Petitions were severally ordered to lie upon the Table, until the Report be received from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the several Persons whose Names are thereunto subscribed, in Behalf of themselves and others residing near, or frequently travelling, the Roads therein-after mentioned, is referred.

A State of the Matter of Fact contained in the said Petition, is as follows:

Mr. Robert Mackafon informed your Committee; That a Precept was issued to the High Constable of the Hundred of Godley, in the County of Surrey, to summon the Innkeepers, Publicans, and Victuallers, of the said Hundred, to attend the Justices, at the King's-Head Inn, at Chert fey, on the ill September following, to take out Licences for selling Ale and Beer; which Precept was

Vol. 34.

took out One of the said Licences, which he carried, on the 30th of November lait, to the proper Officer of the Excise, then at the Crown Inn, at Chertsey, in order to obtain a Licence for retailing Spirituous Liquors; who told him. That his V iCtuallers Licence was good for nothing, and that lie was liable to an Information even' Day, as his Licence was not legally signed. Sir Joseph Maivbey being incapacitated from signing the lame, by an Act made in the Twenty-sixth Year of the Reign of fiis late Majesty.

Mr. John Atkyns, and Mr. William Burton, both Victuallers within the said Hundred, being examined, informed your Committee, That they had applied in like Manner to the Officer of Excise, and had been refused Licences for the same Reason: And Mr. Burton added, that all the Victuallers in the said Hundred of Godley were in the same Circumstances.

An Act of the Twenty-sixth Year of his late Majesty’s Reign was then read; whereby it appeared, that no Justice of the Peace being a Common Brewer of Ale or Beer, Innkeeper, or Distiller, or other Seller of, or Dealer in Ale or any Kind of Spirituous Liquors, or interested in any of the said Trades or Businesses, or being a Victualler or Maltster, shall be capable, or have any Power to grant any Licence or Licences, to any Person or Persons whatsoever, for selling Ale or Beer, or any other Liquots, by Retail; and in case any such Justice or Justices shall grant any such licence, the same shall be null and void, to all Intents and Purposes whatsoever.

Then Sir Joseph Mawbey, Baronet, informed your Committee, That he is concerned in a Corn Distillery, but that the Spirits he fells are not fit for drinking, in the State in which he fells them, but are sold to Compound or Rectifying Distillers, who, he apprehends, distil. them twice more before they are fit for drinking; and that he scarce ever fells a smaller Quantity than Onb Tun, generally Two at a Time; and that the Price of a Tun of such Spirits, at this Time, is £.66.

And Sir Joseph Mawbey further informed your Committee, That hearing, for the first Time, on the 30th of November last, that Mr. Thomas Collector of Ex-

cife for Surrey Collection, had refused to grant the Spirituous Liquor Licence, he applied, on Behalf of the Victuallers, to tire said Mr. Butfian, then at the Excise Office at Chertsey, and was told by him, that he could not grant the Licences, for the Reason before mentioned.

And another Act, made in the Twenty-sixth Year of his late Majesty’s Reign, was also read; which recites an Act of the Second Year of his said Majesty’s Reign, whereby Licences to keep a Common Inn, or Alehouse, or to retail any Brandy, ox strong Waters, may be granted at any general Meeting or the Justices of the Peace acting for the Division where the Person applying for such Licence dwells, to be holden on the First Day of September yearly, or within Twenty Days after, or at any other general Meeting of the said Justices;

A Petition of Aboan Fitzmaurice, Gentleman.

And the said Petition was read; Setting forth, That the Petitioner is the only brother, and nearest Relation Jiving, of Ulysses Fitzmaurice, Esquire, late Lieutenant

Governor of His Majesty’s Island of Saint Vincent, deceased, whose Estates are escheated to the Crown; and that the Petitioner, having subsisted principally by the Brotherly Generality of the said Governor, and relinquished his Occupations here with a View to make a Voyage to Dominica, upon the Intelligence of his Brother’s Death, was soon reduced to Distress; and that the Petitioner applied for Relief to the Commissioners of His Majesty’s Treasury, who appointed the Right honourable Colonel Barre, and the honourable Mr. Fitzmaurice, Administrators to the Personal Estate of the Deceased, and recommended the Petitioner’s same to them; and that the Petitioner, already deprived of the Provision made for him by the Will of the late Earl of Kerry, for want of Means to assert his Claim, is threatened with a limilar Addition to the Loss of his Brother, by the Bill depending for diverting out of the Crown the Estate of the said Ulysses Fitzmaurice; the Purport of which being, that the Public Money accruing from this Escheat should be applied according to Instructions said to have been given by the Deceased for making his Will; and that the Residue, which will be more than Three Fourths of the Whole, should be distributed to other poor Relations of the Intestate’s Mother; the Petitioner, though a Brother, would receive comparatively much less than the Coulin Germans, and the most distant Relations would be better provided for than the nearest; which is contrary to the Disposition of his said Brother, who uniformly distinguished the Petitioner by an affectionate Correspondence, and a generous Contribution to his Subsistence, and whose long and faithful Services, he hopes, will enhance the Petitioner’s Right to greater Bounty; and that from those Considerations, and in consequSftce of the usual Line in which escheated Fortunes are by Royal Bounty permitted to defeend, the Petitioner prays the House, That, after the Payment of the Bequest directed to be given to James, Robert, and John, Fitzmaurice, the Surplus shall belong to the Peti-

VOL. 34.

tioner, or; if the House should think proper to extend Parliamentary Bounty to the most distant Relations of the Deceased on his Mother’s Side, that they will not exclude the Orphan Representative (named John -'maurice) of another Brother on his Father’s Side; and that the Petitioner may be heard, either by himself or Counsel, against such Parts of the said Bill as affect his Interest therein.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the Committee of the whole House, to whom the Bill for diverting out of the Crown the Plantation and Estate of Utyjjes Fitzmaurice, Esquire, deceased, and for veiling the same in Trustees, to be sold, for Payment of his Debts; and for other Purposes therein mentioned, is committed; and that the Petitioner be heard, by himself or Counsel, upon his Petition, if he thinks fit.

Ordered, That it be an Instruction to the said Committee, that they do admit Counsel to be heard, at the same Time, in Favour of the said Bill, against the said Petition.

And then the House adjourned till Monday Morning next, Ten of the Clock.

A Petition of the Merchants, Manufacturers, and Tradesmen, in Behalf of themselves and others, of the City of Norwich, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Petitioners are informed Application is intended to be made, for laying additional Duties on the Importation of Foreign Linens from Germany and other Parts, to which great Quantities of the Woollen and Worsted Manufactures of the said City have for many Years been exported; and representing to the House, that the Exports to Foreign Parts, of the Woollen and Worsted Manufactures have of late Years veiy much declined: And therefore praying. That the Petitioners may be heard, by themselves or Counsel, against any Thing that may be attempted, which may aftect their Manufactories, in the declining and critical State of their Foreign Trade.

A Petition of the Gentlemen, Merchants, Manufacturers, and others, concerned in the Woollen Trade, of the Boroughs of Launcejlonand Newport, in the County of Cornwall, was also presented to the House, and read

Setting forth. That the Petitioners understand a Bill is intended to be brought in, to lay an additional Duty on all German Linens; and representing to the House, that if any further Burthen should be laid on the Importation of Foreign Linens, it must materially affect and injure the Woollen Trade of this Kingdom in general, and particularly distress the poor Inhabitants of the said. Boroughs: And therefore praying the House to take those alarming Consequences under their Consideration.

A Petition of the Merchants, Factors, and Manufacturers of the Town of Birmingham, in the County of Warwick, was also presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Petitioners observe, by the Votes, that Application has been made, for laying an additional Duty upon the Importation of Foreign Linens, and for diminishing the Drawbacks upon their Exportation; and that a considerable Part of the Manufactures of the said Town and Neighourhood have been for many Years, and still are, exported to those Countries where such Linens are made and fold; and should any new Burthen be added thereto, the Petitioners apprehend that such heavy Duties will be inrpoled

Abroad, on the Goods made here, as will give great Advantage to some Manufactories established in Germany similar to their own, and occasion the Loss of a Branch of Trade very interesting to this Kingdom as well^as themselves, and on which many Thousands of their Poor depend for a Subsistence: The Petitioners therefore hope the House will take their same into Consideration, before they come to any Resolution of increasing the Duty already laid upon Foreign Linens, or of diminishing the Drawback.

A Petition of the Linen Manufacturers in Cleveland, in the North Riding, in the County of York, was also presented to the House, and read; Complaining of the Decline of the Linen Manufacture, which, the Petitioners alledge, is owing to the increasefi Importation of Foreign Linen: And therefore praying the House to take the Premises under a solid Consideration, and to pass such Laws as may seem belt adapted for the Encouragement of the Home Manufacture of Linen, and to give such other Relief as to the House shall seem proper.

A Petition of the Mayor, Capital Burgesses, Merchants, FaC^jfs, and Manufacturers, of the Borough of

Walsall, in the County of Stafford, and also of the Factors and Manufacturers of the Towns of and Darlaston, in the said County of Stafford, was also

presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Petitioners are informed, it is intended to lay an additional £)uty upon Foreign Linens imported, and to lessen the Drawbacks of all such Linens upon Exportation; and that the greatest Part of the Manufactures of the said Towns are exported to Germany, and other Parts of the Continent, where such Foreign Linens are made and imported into this Kingdom; and that, if any additional Duties should be laid on Foreign Linens imported, or any Burthens or Restrictions upon the Exportation thereof, the Petitioners are informed. Foreign Powers will impose such heavy Duties upon the Goods and Manufactures made here, as will give great Advantage to Numbers of similar Manufactories established in Germany and many other Parts of the Continent, which will be very injurious and detrimental to the Trade and Manufactures of this Kingdom in general,- and of the Petitioners in particular: And therefore praying the House will take these alarming Consequences into Consideration, and give them such Relief in the Premises as shall appear reasonable.

A Petition of the Merchants, Factors, and Manufacturers, of the Towns of Wolverhampton, Bilstone, and Willenhall, in the County of Stafford, was also presented to the House, and read; setting forth. That the Petitioners observe, by the Votes, that Application is made, for laying an additional Duty upon Foreign Linens on Importation into this Kingdom, and lowering the Drawback upon the Exportation; and that a . great Part of the Manufactures of the said Places and Neighbourhood have been many Years exported to the Countries where such Linens are fabricated, and should any new Duty be laid upon the Imports of such Linens, and the Drawback oq Exportation lessened, the Petitioners have lteafpn to think that such heavy Duties will be imposed Abroad, on the Goods made here, as will immediately decrease our Demands, and in Time occasion the Loss of a Trade highly interesting to this Kingdom as well as themselves, and on which many Thousands of their industrious Poor depend for a Subsistence: And therefore, praying the House to take their same into Consideration, before any Alteration is made on the Duties or Drawback already established.

A Petition of the several Persons whose Names ai*e thereunto subscribed, being divers of the Directors, Trustees, and Members, of a Society, called " The " Laudable Society for the Benefit of Widows," on Behalf of themselves and the major Part of the Members of the said Society, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the Petitioners observe, by the Votes, that a Petition has been presented, for Leave to bring in a Bill to compel the present Trustees, who now reside in England, to fell the Capital Stock of the said Society; and that the fame, and such other Monies as belong to the Society, and shall be in the Hands of the Secretary, may be divided amongst the Annuitants and the rest of the Proprietors, in Proportion to their respective Claims and Interests; and that the Petitioners apprehend, that the Plan on which the said Society is now formed, is fully adequate to answer all the Purposes for which it was instituted, the Capital at this Time greatly- increasing; and that, if any Deficiency should happen in the Fund appropriated for Payment of the Widows who become chargeable on the Society, there is an amplti Provision made for the fame, by the Articles entered into by all the Members of the Society; and that the said Society is formed upon the rood benevolent Principles, for the Benefit of the Widows of a Class of Men, many of whom have no other Means of making a suitable Provision for them: And therefore praying, That the Bill for enabling the said Trustees to fell the Capital Stock, and dividing the Money belonging to the Laid Society, may not pass into a Law; and that no Alteration may be made in the present Plan of the said Society; and that the Petitioners may be heard, by their Counsel, against the said Bill.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Confederation of the Committee, to whom the Petition of the several Persons whose Names are subscribed, being divers of the Directors, Trustees, and Members, of the Laudable Society for the Benefit of Widows, is referred; and that the Petitioners be heard, by their Counsel, before the said Committee, upon their Petition, if they think fit.

Ordered, That it be an Instruction to the said Committee, that they do admit Counsel to be heard, at the same Time, in Favour of the said former Petition* against the Petition now presented.

A Petition of the Right honourable Barbara Countels Dowager of Bo wls, in Behalf of the Right honourable George Edward Henry Arthur Earl of Powis, her Son, now an Infant, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth. That the Petitioner, on the 28th of February last, offered a Petition to the House, representing, that the late Henry Arthur Earl of Powis, dee'eased. Father of the said present Earl, having, not long before his Decease, become seised in Fee of several Lands, Tenements, and Hereditaments, in the Counties of Montgomery and Salop, or one of them, heretofore the real Estates of Charles Mason, Esquire, deceased, patented a Memorial to the Lords Commissioners of the Treasury, thereby praying their Lordships to permit him to compound a certain Claim of the Crown, in the said Memorial stated to affeift the said real Estates, on such Terms as to the said Commissioners should seem meet; and that the said Memorial being referred by the said Commissioners to the Solicitor of the Treasury, to consider the fame, and to report to their Lordships a State of the Cafe, with his Opinion thereon, the Solicitor of the Treasury, by his Report, bearing Date the 24th Day of November 1772, certified to the said Commissioners, that, by a Decree in the Court of Chancer)', made on the 9th Day of December 1713, between Sir By by Lake, Baronet, Plaintiff, and joseph Newell, and

George Newell, and others, Defendants, it appeared, that

the said Masons Estates in Montgomery and were mortgaged to the said Sir By by Lake, for several large Sums of Money, and that the said Mason was indebted to her late Majesty Queen in it large Sum -issued him, on Account of her Majesty’s Service, as Paymaster of the Transports, in which Tran! ad ions the said Newells had been concerned; and that the said Court of Chancery did, by the said Decree, direct an Account should be taken of what was due to the said Sir By by Lake on his several Mortgages, and also of all Transactions between the said Newells and the said Mason; and, if any thing should be found due to the said Newells, the same should be raised and paid out of the said mortgaged Premises, after Payment of the said Lake's Incumbrances, and be applied towards Satisfaction of what was due from them to the Crown; and the said Solicitor of the Treasury further certified, that, by the Mailer’s Report in the said Cause, dated the 26th Day of June 1770, it appeared there was then due to Byby Lake, Esquire, the legal Representative of the said Sir Byby Lake, on his said Mortgages, for Principal, interest, and Colls, 38,441/. z /. 4 </.; and that, by an Account of the Receiver of the said mortgaged Premises, passed in the Court of Chancery, for One Year ending Lady Day 1768, the yearly Value of the same Premises in Montgomery and was only

1,104/. 15*- to d.;wherefore the said Solicitor of the Treasury submitted to "the Confederation of the said. Commissioners, that, under the Circumstances of the Cafe, and particularly in regard the said mortgaged Premises, if fold, would not fell for nearly the Sum reported due to the said Lake, the Claim the

Crown had thereon could never be satisfied; therefore "the Solicitor of the Treasury was of Opinion, that the said Commissioners might properly consent to the said Estates being discharged from the said Debt due to the Crown; but as it appeared, from the Proceedings in the said Cause in Chancery, that the Solicitor of the Taxes had had the foie Management of the Crown’s interest, he submitted it to the Lords Commissioners, whether it would be proper to direct the Matter of the said Memorial to belaid before the Solicitor of the Tax Office, who would be better able to advise their Lordships, whether any or what Composition ought to be paid; and that the said Report of the Solicitor of the Treasury having by the said Lords Commissioners been referred to the Solicitor of the Tax Office, to report his Opinion on the said Report-, the Solicitor of the Tax Office, by his Report to the Lords Commissioners of the Treasury, dated-the Second Da)' of July 1773, certified to their Lordships, that the Fadls stated in the Report of the said Solicitor to the Treasury, with regard to the Debt due to Mr. Lake therein mentioned, and with regard to the annual Value of the said mortgaged Premises, were truly stated; wherefore he was of Opinion, that the interest of the Mortgage to Mr. Lake (whose Debt was prior to that of the Crown) greatly exceeded the Income of the mortgaged Estate, and of Consequence that Mr. Lake's Debt did annually increase; and that he was of Opinion, the Debt due to Mr. Lake much exceeded the intrinsic Value of the mortgaged Estate; and as it would not, in his Opinion, be adviseable for the Crown to redeem the said Mortgage, he thought it might be proper for their Lordships to permit the then Petitioner to apply to Parliament to enable their Lordships to compound the Debt due to the Crown; and after such Act should be obtained, their Lordships might compound the said Debt for such Sum of Money as, under all Circumstances of the Cafe, they should think reasonable; but he was of Opinion, their Lordships could not compound the same without the Aid of Parliament; and that the said George Edward Henry Arthur Earl of Powis, on the Death of his late Father, became, and is now, intitled to the said Estates of the said Charles Mason, whereof his said Father was seised as aforesaid; and although no Benefit can ever

.merican A Petition of William Bollan, Esquire, Agent for the

'olonies. Council of the Province of Bay, in

England, was presented to the House, and read; Setting forth, That the English American Colonies were deduced and planted by the Adventurers and Settlers, at their Expence, in Foreign inhospitable Lands, acquired by their vigorous Efforts, made under the Authority of their Princes, granted with the Encouragement proper for this spirited and noble Enterprize; and that the several Princes, by whose Authority the Colonies were established, and the numerous Nobles and other worthy Persons, of whom several were Men of the

VOL. 34.

greatest Accomplillmients, endued with the Wisdom proper for obtaining and preserving Empire, by whole Advice, Aid, and Concurrence, they were undertaken and advanced, were so far from understanding that these Adventurers and Settlers, who, by their Travail, Expences, Labours, and Dangers, should enlarge the public Dominion, should thereby, contrary to natural Justice, lessen their public Liberties; that, from the many Letters Patent Royal, made and paffld for obtaining and regulating new Dominion, and the whole History of their Settlement, it manifestly appears, it was the Intent of all Parties, that the Settlers and their Posterity should enjoy the fame; whereupon they became Adventurers; and, inspirited by their Confidence therein* with their long and quiet Enjnyifient of their public Rights, overcoming Difficulties, Perils, and Hardships, inexpressible and innumerable, they raised the King’s American Empire out of a dreary and dangerous Wilderness, with so great and continual Increase of Commerce, that of late Years it hath given Employment unto Two Thirds of the British Shipping, with a comfortable Support to no small Part of the Inhabitants of Great Britain, and great Addition to the Dignity and Strength of its Naval Empire; and that, by the Statute Law of this Kingdom, it is clearly supposed, and in effect fully declared, that the Colonists were well entitled to the English Right, and the Lands they inhabit free; and that the A£la Regia of Queen Elizabeth and her Successors, whereby the Acquests of new Dominion were made and established, and Security given to the Adventurers, Planters, and their Descendants, of the perpetual Enjoyment of their public Liberties, having, as the Petitioner presumes, never been laid before the House, nor the Colonies ever yet had any Opportunity to ascertain and defend their invaluable Rights, and the House, as the Petitioner is advised, now having under their Consideration the State of the Northern Colonies; the Petitioner therefore prays. That he may be permitted to appear, and lay before the House authentic Copies of the proper AEla Regia, and to support the Matters herein contained, in a Manner suitable to their Nature, and the Inclinations of the House.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

Ordered, That the Order of the Day, for taking into further Consideration His Majesty’s most gracious Mef-sage of Monday last, together with the Papers which were presented to the House by the Lord North, upon the yth and nth Days of this Instant March, by His Majesty’s Command, be now read.

Linen A Petition of the Clothiersand Traders in the Woollen

(Ilmlfter,) Manufactory, living and residing in and near the Town of Ilmifter, in the County of Somerftt, was presented to the House, and read; Setting Forth, That the Woollen Trade hath for some Years past been very bad; and that there is almost a total Stagnation of that Branch of Trade in the said County; and that the Petitioners are informed, that some Regulations are intended to be made, by putting an additional Duty upon Foreign Linens, which would greatly affect, injure, and prejudice, the Staple of England: And therefore praying, That such intended Regulations of the Foreign Linfifi Trade may not in any wise affect, prejudice, or injure, the Staple of this Nation.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the Committee of the whole House, to whom it is referred to enquire further into the present State of the Linen Trade in Great Britain and Ireland.

Mr. Williams reported from the Committee, to whom the<Petition of Sir Roger Mofiy Baronet, Lord of the Manor of Neston and Leighton, and John Glegg, Esquire, Lord of the Manor of Gayton, in the County of Chester, was referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of Fast contained in the said Petition, and had directed him to report the State thereof to the House; and he read the Report in his Place, and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk’s Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

A State o? the Matter of Fast, contained in the said Petition, is as follows:

Mr. William Alder oft, being examined, laid. He knows the said Manors; that Stones and Gravel have been carried away from many Parts of them, which lie next the Sea, by which a great deal of Land has been washed away; that some Roads have been destroyed within the said Manors, by being undermined by the Sea; that great Damage has been done to Two Fields in particular; and that, unless the Practice of gathering and carrying away Stones and Gravel on the Sea Shores there be flopped, a great Quantity of Land will be either washed away or overflowed; that he has known the Lands 28 Years, and that the above-mentioned Damage has been done within the last Two or Three Years.

Ordered, That it be an Instruction.to the Committee, to whom the Bill to prevent the taking and carrying away of Stones from the Sea Shore, below High-Water Mark, between Orms Head, in the County of Carnarvon, and the River at Voryd, is committed, that they have Power to make Provision in the said Bill, for the preventing the taking away Stones from the Shore, in the Manors of Neston, Leighton, and Gayton, on the opposite Side of the River Dee, in the County of Chester.

A Petition of the Merchants, Traders, and Manu- Linen Trade, fasturers of the Town of Paisley, was presented to the House, and read; Complaining of the Decline of the Linen and Thread Manufactures, which, the Petitioners alledge, is the Cause of many Thousands of His Majesty’s Subjects being reduced to the utmost Distress for Want of Employ, and many Hundreds of them have been obliged to emigrate from the said Town to distant Countries, to prevent them from starving: And therefore praying the House to take this important Affair into their Consideration, and grant such Relief as to them shall seem meet.

A Petition of the Linen Manufactures at North Aller- Ditto. ton, and Bromton, in the County of York, was allb pre- (North fented to the House, and read; likewise complaining of the Decline of the Linen Manufacture in that Part of the Nation; which is owing, as the Petitioners apprehend, to the Importation of Foreign Linen: And therefore praying the House to take the Premises into Consideration, and to pass such Laws as may seem bell adapted for the Encouragement of the Home Manufacture of Linen, and to give such other Relief as to the House shall seem proper.
